name: Gresham
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Gresham, OR 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Gresham, OR: the Parade of Lights and Arts Plaza tree lighting, Breakfast with Santa, reindeer in Rockwood and free Santa photos.
lede: Gresham does Christmas downtown and in Rockwood: a Parade of Lights that brings Santa to the Arts Plaza, a 60-foot living ponderosa pine lit up for the season, and reindeer visits at Rockwood Market Hall.
celebrates: The big night is Spirit of Christmas, run by Spirit of Gresham, the holiday events arm of the Center for the Arts Foundation, with the City of Gresham. The day starts with Breakfast with Santa at the Little Theatre on Main Avenue, then North Pole Village activities and a holiday market fill historic downtown. At dusk the Parade of Lights carries Santa down Main Avenue to the Gresham Arts Plaza for the tree lighting and free Santa photos. In Rockwood, Rockwood Market Hall holds a Winter Festival with its own tree lighting, and Gresham Parks and Recreation brings Santa's reindeer there in December. Gresham Station adds free Santa photos and a SnowCap food drive.
lastyear: In 2025 Spirit of Christmas took place on Saturday, December 6, the second year it was hosted by Spirit of Gresham. The Outlook reported that hundreds of families came downtown for the Parade of Lights, presented by Gresham Ford, and the lighting of the 60-foot living ponderosa pine in the Arts Plaza. Santa and Mrs. Claus arrived on the Weston Kia Antique Fire Truck and flipped the switch, and Councilor Keathley called it the largest crowd yet.
facts: Gresham is named after Walter Quintin Gresham, a Civil War general who became United States Secretary of State. The town stayed unincorporated until 1905, the year of Portland's Lewis and Clark Centennial Exposition, when it had just 365 residents. By the 2020 census Gresham had 114,247 people, making it the fourth most populous city in Oregon. Its Christmas tree is not a cut tree at all but a living ponderosa pine about 60 feet tall in the Arts Plaza.
trains: Gresham is the end of the line for the MAX Blue Line. The light rail between Portland and Gresham opened on September 5, 1986, and about 250,000 people came to three days of opening celebrations. Today Blue Line trains stop at Rockwood/East 188th Avenue, Civic Drive, Gresham City Hall and Gresham Central Transit Center before ending at Cleveland Avenue. From downtown Gresham, families can ride MAX into Portland for the Holiday Express at the Oregon Rail Heritage Center or the Washington Park and Zoo Railway.

traditions: Cars strung with lights carry Santa down Main Avenue to the Gresham Arts Plaza.
The 60-foot living ponderosa pine in the Arts Plaza lights up right after the parade and stays lit through the holidays.
Pancakes with Santa and friends at the Little Theatre on Main Avenue open the Spirit of Christmas day.
Gresham Parks and Recreation brings Santa's reindeer, crafts and a Letters to Santa station to Rockwood Market Hall.
Rockwood Market Hall lights its own tree with free kids crafts and a wreath workshop using native Oregon plants.
Holiday events around Gresham invite families to bring food for SnowCap's Fill-A-Bag drive.
kidfact: Gresham's Christmas tree is alive. It is a ponderosa pine about 60 feet tall that grows right in the Arts Plaza, so it gets decorated year after year instead of being cut down.
faq: Where is the Gresham Christmas tree lighting?

Gresham lights its tree at the Gresham Arts Plaza, 401 NE 2nd Street, during Spirit of Christmas on the first Saturday of December. The tree is a living ponderosa pine about 60 feet tall. The Parade of Lights brings Santa down Main Avenue to the plaza just before the lighting, and free Santa photos follow.
Who runs Spirit of Christmas in Gresham?

Spirit of Gresham, the holiday events arm of the Center for the Arts Foundation, hosts it with the City of Gresham. The day includes Breakfast with Santa at the Little Theatre, North Pole Village activities and a holiday market downtown, the Parade of Lights presented by Gresham Ford, the tree lighting and Santa photos.
Can kids meet reindeer in Gresham?

Yes. Gresham Parks and Recreation holds Reindeer in Rockwood at Rockwood Market Hall each December, with reindeer, treats, crafts and a Letters to Santa station where kids who write their name and address get a reply. Gresham Station also hosts a reindeer meet and greet on a December weekend.
Can we get to Gresham's Christmas events by train?

Yes. The MAX Blue Line runs from downtown Portland through Rockwood to Gresham, stopping at Rockwood/East 188th Avenue, Civic Drive, Gresham City Hall and Gresham Central Transit Center before it ends at Cleveland Avenue. Rockwood Market Hall is on SE 185th Avenue in the Rockwood neighborhood, and the Arts Plaza is in historic downtown Gresham.
